Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

1. This appeal is filed by the claimant against the judgment and award dated 04.06.2020 passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.-XII, Vijayapura [for short 'Tribunal'] in MVC No.486/2020 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The injured claimant aged 60 years, met with an accident on 17.01.2020 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, she filed claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.16,50,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.3,17,331/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization NC: 2025:KHC-K:7027 HC-KAR and directed respondent-NEKRTC to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant-claimant has preferred this appeal.

3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4.
The main contention of the appellant/claimant is that, the Tribunal has awarded meagre compensation under all heads.

It is contended by the learned counsel for claimant that as per Ex.P5 - Wound Certificate the claimant sustained fracture of left side fibula and fracture of right medial malleolus, for which, she was hospitalized for 15 days and underwent operations and spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical expenses and discharged with advise to follow up treatment and another major surgery for which she needs Rs.1,50,000/-.
He states that the PW2-Doctor has assessed permanent disability at 20 to 25% each relating to right and left lower limbs.
It is contended that the claimant was aged 60 years and by doing tailoring work she was earning Rs.15,000/- per NC: 2025:KHC-K:7027 HC-KAR month.

He submitted that due to injuries,
claimant has 100% functional disability and thus, requested for enhancing the compensation with 9% interest per annum.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondent contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference.

6. As per Ex.P5 - Wound Certificate, the claimant had sustained fracture of left fibula distal end,
fracture of right medial malleolous.

PW2 - Doctor has observed existence of operative scar marks over left ankle region, and swelling and deformity over both ankles and restrictions of movement of both ankle terminally by 10 to 15 degree.
PW2 has stated that claimant unable to sit and squat properly with cross leg and she walks with limp on her left side.
Observing all these aspect, he issued Disability Certificate as per Ex.P12 stating that the claimant sustained permanent disability of 20 to 25% to left lower limb and 20 to 25% to right lower limb.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7027 HC-KAR
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take 17% functional disability to the claimant.
7. Though, the claimant states that she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, she has not produced any document to prove the same.

As the accident is of the year 2020, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant at Rs.13,750/- per month, which needs no interference.
As per Wound Certificate - Ex.P5 claimant was aged 65 years at the time of accident and the Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of '7'.

Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for loss of future earning as under:
Rs.13,750/- x 12 x 7 x 17 % = Rs.1,96,350/-
8.
The claimant was admitted in the hospital for 15 days.

Considering the period of hospitalization,
nature of injuries and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain NC: 2025:KHC-K:7027 HC-KAR and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.

Further,
due to injuries the claimant might not have attended any work atleast for a period of 3 months,
hence, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.41,250/- for loss of income during laid up period.
However, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.52,331/- for medical expenses and Rs.15,000/- for future medical expenses needs no interference.
9.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
( ii )
The claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.92,600/- with NC: 2025:KHC-K:7027 HC-KAR interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(iii) Respondent - NEKRTC is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
